page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ecs.se1 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores running at 2.5 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.se1.xlarge exhibits modest performance characteristics. In CPU-focused evaluations, the instance achieved a single-core stress-ng score of 1100.49 and a multi-core score of 2931.93, both placing in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 163.82 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 20.19 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, reflecting lower-tier throughput. Real-world simulation benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core (918.0) and multi-core (1990.0), as well as Passmark database operations (1073.82), consistently rank in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested systems.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1.xlarge is its high memory allocation relative to its lower-tier processing capabilities. While the 32.0 GB RAM capacity supports memory-intensive workloads, the underlying Intel Xeon processor limits high-throughput compute tasks. This makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound applications that do not require intensive CPU performance, such as caching layers, lightweight database operations, or basic web serving. It is less suitable for compute-heavy tasks like software compilation or complex data processing.
